title: Phased Variant Rollout with Compatibility Hints and Tiered Capacity Routing
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: We need a more expressive rollout primitive that lets Platform and Product teams perform phased rollouts across model variants while encoding lightweight compatibility metadata to allow safe routing and automated demotion when capacity or semantics diverge. Current mechanisms (weighted splits + manual fallbacks) are brittle for heterogeneous variant families (different quantizations, KV cache shapes, or small architecture tweaks) and do not gracefully handle cross-region pressure or cost-tier substitution.

Goal: Implement a rollout and routing policy that supports: (1) phased percentage canaries, (2) A/B/shadow experiment modes, (3) per-variant compatibility hints (fingerprints + semantic contract level), (4) tier-aware routing that prefers low-cost variants for non-SLO workloads and routes to higher tiers for latency-sensitive traffic, and (5) automated rollback/demotion triggers based on SLO regressions, misalignment of compatibility signals, and capacity pressure across regions.

Out of scope: full semantic validation of outputs (evals will remain in Redwood Optimize), and on-prem install automation for the private control plane (follow-up project).
acceptance_criteria: Platform exposes a rollout config schema allowing: phases (percent), mode (canary|ab|shadow), compatibility_hints (fingerprint, contract_level, kv_shape_hash), and tier_routing_policy (prefer_cost_tier, strict_affinity)

Runtime honors routing policy in production for a sample customer (internal test account) and routes traffic according to percent splits and tier preferences for at least two variants (v2-quantized, v2-fp16).

Automated demotion/rollback runs when latency P95 increases by >30% or token error rate exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive minutes; incident triggers a canary rollback and creates a runbook entry in PagerDuty test channel.
Region failover: when a region's GPU utilization crosses 85% for >120s, routing moves non-critical tiers to alternative regions respecting data residency labels; verified by chaos test script.
Console UI shows per-variant compatibility score and current tier routing percentages; relevant metrics available in the Rollouts dashboard (latency, cost per-token, error-rate).
Unit/integration tests for routing policy compiler and compatibility-hint matching with >90% coverage for new modules.
tasks: Design rollout config schema and examples (Kunal) - write PRD and JSON schema
Implement runtime router changes to accept compatibility_hints and cost_tier routing (Eng: runtime team)
Add automatic demotion circuit-breaker with hysteresis (SLO team)
Console: show variant compatibility score and edit percent splits (DX team)
Create canary & regional chaos test harness + dashboards (Reliability)
Security review for compatibility metadata and routing policy (Security)
Docs: update rollout and routing docs, include example rollback runbook (Docs)
Integration test: simulate mixed-traffic (shadow + normal) and verify fallback (QA)
implementation_notes: Compatibility hint model: short fingerprint (sha1 of serialized model metadata), contract_level enum (strict|compatible|best-effort), kv_shape_hash optional for KV cache compatibility.
Router will reject routing to a variant if contract_level==strict and serving_path does not advertise compatible kv_shape_hash; for compatible/best-effort route anyway but tag metric for drift.
Tiered routing: allow policies like prefer_cost_tier: ['low','medium'] with a fallback list; critical paths will set strict_affinity:true to prevent lower-tier substitution.
Automated demotion: monitored signals are token-P95 latency, client-visible error-rate, and model-output regression score (if available). Thresholds are configurable per-rollout.
We will store rollout configs as namespaced objects in control plane backed by Postgres with optimistic concurrency for edits. Consider using existing rollout history tables for auditability.
test_plan: Unit tests for routing compiler and compatibility matcher
Integration test: create rollout with 5% canary -> 20% -> 100% and validate metrics & automated demotion only triggers on injected failures
Chaos test: simulate regional capacity pressure and assert tiered traffic shifts to alternate regions while keeping privacy labels intact
Shadow-to-production test: verify shadow traffic does not affect quota or cost-tier promotions and that shadow logs are visible in Rollouts dashboard
Manual acceptance: PM + Reliability run through playbook with internal customer and confirm console UI and rollback behavior
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-eager automated rollback could flip-flop on noisy telemetry. Mitigation: implement hysteresis, minimum evaluation window (3m) and require two independent signals before rollback.

Risk: Compatibility fingerprints may be miscomputed for models produced by third-party conversion tools. Mitigation: provide a compatibility verification job that can be run pre-rollout and surfaced in the Console.
Risk: Cross-region routing may violate data residency constraints. Mitigation: enforce data residency labels on rollout configs and validate in the routing compiler.
Risk: Increased control-plane write volume from many concurrent rollout edits. Mitigation: rate-limit edits per-org and batch background propagation to downstream routers.
observability: New Rollouts dashboard with: per-variant traffic %, P95 latency, cost-per-token estimate, compatibility mismatch rate
Tracer tags: rollout_id, phase, variant_fingerprint, tier_hint
Alerting rules: P95 latency > baseline*1.3 for 3m triggers investigate; compatibility_mismatch_rate > 0.5% triggers warn
Audit log entry for each rollout config change with user, diff, and timestamp
console_changes: Variant panel: show compatibility fingerprint + contract level and a link to compatibility verification report
Rollout editor: allow step definitions with percent, duration, and tier preferences
Quick rollback button with reason dropdown (SLO-regression, compatibility-drift, capacity-pressure) that triggers demote to previous stable variant
migration_notes: Existing weighted-split rollouts will continue to work. Add migration script to backfill compatibility_hints as 'best-effort' for current variants.
Add a nightly job to compute KV shape hashes for models that expose KV metadata; surface results in the model catalog for onboarding teams.
